title: Product definition
description: Define a scoped product problem, evidence-backed requirements, user flows, feasibility, and acceptance criteria.
intent: Produce the requested product definition or assessment from accepted goals and real evidence. Return decision-ready artifacts; implementation, tracker changes, recruitment, and publication are not implied.

assignments.task: Establish the problem, users, constraints, current behavior, assumptions, and decision/acceptance criteria.
Analyze supplied user evidence or propose a bounded study; distinguish assumptions from observed needs.
assignments.when: User needs or usability evidence are material to the decision.

assignments.task: Gather current supporting or contradictory market/technical sources.
assignments.when: External or current facts materially affect the requirements.

assignments.task: Assess consequential contracts, boundaries, dependencies, and feasibility.
assignments.when: The proposal affects architecture, persistence, integrations, or substantial technical constraints.

assignments.task: Define measurable baselines/outcomes from actual approved data or identify missing measurement.
assignments.when: Success metrics or existing behavior data are part of the task.

assignments.task: Reconcile evidence into bounded requirements, priorities, edge cases, and testable acceptance criteria.
Develop or assess complete task flows, information hierarchy, transitions, continuity, and recovery requirements against the completed evidence brief.
Check requirements for testability, contradictions, missing edge cases, and feasible acceptance evidence.
Check material factual/quantitative claims and the distinction between assumptions and findings.
assignments.when: The deliverable relies on consequential factual or quantitative claims.

assignments.task: Review completed flow/requirements for visual-system, component, state, and responsive alignment.
assignments.when: The proposal includes concrete UI/component choices.

completion: The product problem, bounded requirements, and acceptance criteria are explicit and evidence-linked.
Design and feasibility decisions reflect the completed evidence brief; unresolved dependencies and assumptions remain explicit.
No source implementation or external operation is inferred from a product-definition request.
